the teachers in the classrooms we observed were not able to deal effectively with the diversity of their students, and that the conflict discourse they employed was not helpful to their students in terms of developing an inclusive approach to diversity.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we need to rethink our approach to diversity and conflict and to consider how they can be integrated in the classroom in a meaningful way, so that they do not reproduce stereotypes and prejudices, but can become a resource for learning.

the study of diversity in the context of conflict is a useful way of examining the ways in which the conflict is reproduced and/or challenged, and how the boundaries of ‘us’ are negotiated in a divided context.

the findings suggest that teachers’ awareness of their own and their students’ identities and of the ways in which conflict is represented in the classroom, are important factors in the construction of a conflict-sensitive pedagogy.
The main takeaway from our work is that

teachers should be more sensitive about the ways they talk and write about the conflict, and that they should be encouraged to develop a more critical stance towards the ways they represent ‘others’, and particularly, those who are different from them in the conflict context.
diversity is a resource, which needs to be harnessed and used to promote social cohesion in the face of conflict.
teachers need to be aware of the potential for conflict in their classroom and to be prepared to address it in a way that is sensitive to the needs of all their students.
